MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT
I. PRELIMINARY STATEMENT
This Court should grant plaintiff's Motion for Partial Summary Judgment on the first claim for possession in plaintiff's Complaint because there is no genuine issue of material fact. III. LAW AND ARGUMENT
A. Motion for Summary Judgment Standard
The Ohio Rules of Civil Procedure provide under Civ.R 56(C) that summary judgment is proper if "the pleadings, depositions, answers to interrogatories, written admissions, affidavits, transcripts of evidence, and written stipulations of fact, if any ... show that there is no genuine issue as to any material fact and that the moving party is entitled to judgment as a matter of law." No genuine issue of material fact exists when "it appears from the evidence that reasonable minds can come to but one conclusion, and viewing such evidence most strongly in favor of the party against whom the motion for summary judgement is made, that conclusion is adverse to that party.
